text: For visualizing the distribution of a continuous measurement across a small number of samples, which plot type does the chapter recommend over a bar chart with error bars?
explanation: For small-n distributions, violin plots or beeswarm plots show the actual shape and spread of the data rather than collapsing it to a single mean and error bar, which can hide bimodality, outliers, or skew. Pie charts are recommended only for parts-of-a-whole (and bar charts are preferred even there), while stacked area charts and 3D bar charts are not recommended at all -- 3D effects in particular are flagged as chartjunk under the data-ink ratio principle.
